title: Captain of boat that capsized near Statue of Liberty charged in deaths of mother and baby
summary: Manuel Hernandez was charged with two counts of misconduct and neglect of a ship officer resulting in death in the accident, which killed Sara Sanchez, 27, and her 5-month-old daughter, Antonella Garcia.
story: The captain of an allegedly unlicensed boat that capsized in New York Harbor near Liberty Island over the weekend, killing a young woman and her baby, has been charged in their deaths.

Manuel Hernandez, 46, was charged Monday with two counts of misconduct and neglect of a ship officer resulting in death, according to a criminal complaint filed in U.S District Court for the Southern District of New York.

Hernandez, of Manville, New Jersey, appeared in court Monday, where he was not required to enter a plea and was released on $50,000 bail, NBC New York reported. He left with his court-appointed attorney, Amy Gallicchio, and both declined to comment, the station reported.
Gallicchio did not immediately respond to a request for comment from NBC News.
Queens resident Sara Sanchez, 27, and her 5-month-old daughter, Antonella Garcia, died in the tragedy Saturday evening.

Hernandez was piloting a Yamaha AR210 jet vessel Saturday night — but he had not registered it, did not have the certification to operate it in the harbor with paying customers and did not have infant-sized flotation devices on board, according to the complaint.
Furthermore, he had 14 people on board, including himself — exceeding the vessel’s maximum capacity of 10 people, the complaint alleges.
The accident
Hernandez operated the vessel while he was working for a tour operations company, which branded itself as a luxury limousine and rental yacht provider.
Saturday’s tour was for 13 passengers for a trip around the harbor near the Statue of Liberty, arranged through the tour operator for $1,800, the complaint said.

Hernandez is alleged to have told law enforcement officers in a post-arrest interview that he had periodically worked for the operator since 2025 and had piloted two similar tours on his personal boat, a Yamaha AR250 — which is similar to but larger than the vessel used in Saturday’s accident.

The night of Saturday’s tour, he used a friend’s boat, as his personal one needed mechanical repairs, but he did not inform the owner he was using it for a tour with paying customers, prosecutors allege in the complaint.

Hernandez told authorities he was unaware of the maximum capacity for the boat he was driving Saturday but knew his personal boat could take no more than 12 passengers, the complaint says. He said he initially believed Saturday’s tour would consist of 12 passengers but ultimately agreed to take 13, according to prosecutors.
The day of the trip, Sanchez was with her 5-month-old baby and the child’s father, whom co-workers identified as Andres Garcia.

Before boarding, Hernandez asked the parents whether they had an infant-sized personal flotation device for the baby, and they said they did not, according to the complaint. He told them the boat was not equipped with a child- or infant-sized personal flotation device and instead said one of them would need to wear a flotation device and hold the baby throughout the tour, which Sanchez did, the complaint alleges.

At 10:20 p.m., three hours and 20 minutes into the tour, Hernandez made a U-turn, which brought the vessel into a swell, which was “possibly caused by the wake of a larger passing vessel,” the complaint says.
“However, the swell swamped the bow of the vessel and immediately capsized the vessel,” according to the filing.
The 13 passengers and Hernandez were all thrown overboard.

Shortly after the capsizing, other boats, including commercial vessels and others operated by the New York Police Department, the Coast Guard and the New York City Fire Department, responded, and 11 passengers and Hernandez were pulled from the water in varying conditions.

The bodies of Sanchez and her baby were recovered in the water by police and members of the Coast Guard. Both were unresponsive. They received CPR and were taken to a hospital in Brooklyn, where they were pronounced dead upon arrival.
Hernandez didn’t have required credentials for the boat, prosecutors allege

The complaint said Hernandez never obtained a merchant mariner credential (MMC) or a valid Coast Guard certificate of inspection, both of which are required to operate a vessel with paying customers on board.
The boat was a type and size that made it ineligible to receive a certificate of inspection for “the type of operation conducted by Hernandez,” the complaint says.

Hernandez admitted to law enforcement that he never sought the certificate of inspection or the MMC, both of which are required under federal regulations, because he was unaware that they were required, the filing says.

The certificate of inspection involves a stability test to determine the total number of passengers allowed on board during for-hire operations. The MMC requires operators to show a minimum of 360 days of documented boating experience, and operators must pass a physical examination, a drug test and a background check, as well as first aid, CPR and boating courses, according to the filing.

Because the boat involved in the accident carried more than six passengers, the bar was even higher, the complaint says: An operator must hold an even higher level of certification than the baseline MMC, including a separate exam on navigation, vessel operation and other safety measures.
It is also mandated that children under 13 must wear appropriate personal flotation devices, the filing says.
A community in mourning
The grieving community is rallying around Sanchez’s partner.

On Monday, the general managers of two businesses he worked at held a news conference to support him. He worked at Il Punto Restaurant, which has locations in Manhattan and Flushing, Queens, and at the Marco Hotel, holding various positions over the past six years.
The general managers described Garcia as Sanchez’s husband and as a hardworking, dedicated family man who supported not only his family in New York but also back in his home country, Colombia.
They started an online fundraiser to support Garcia and their surviving 6-year-old child.
Antonio Russo, the general manager of Il Punto, said that he had asked Garcia to work Saturday night at the Manhattan restaurant but that Garcia surprisingly said no.

“He said: ‘Antonio, would you please mind? I have something planned,’ and I was so happy for him, because he never had anything planned,” Russo said. “And he posted a story on his WhatsApp showing the view from the boat, and we all saw it. We were all surprised that he could actually enjoy a minute of his life, because this guy has been providing for his family here but also for his family in Colombia.”
Russo said he had a conversation with Garcia just one day before the tragedy in which Garcia expressed how happy he felt with his family.

“He told me how blessed he felt to have such a wife ... that he was very grateful to have her and that he felt so lucky and blessed,” Russo recalled. “That was the first time we spoke about this so deeply, and then that happened the day after. Can you imagine?”

title: Lauren Boebert’s 21-year-old son is arrested on child sexual exploitation charges
summary: The allegations are linked to a video Tyler Boebert, then 18, is accused of recording in 2024 with a 17-year-old.
story: The son of Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., was arrested on charges of sexual exploitation of a child, authorities said Monday.
Tyler Boebert, 21, was taken into custody Sunday and later released on $10,000 bond, the Garfield County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement.
Tyler Boebert did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
“I love my son,” Lauren Boebert said in a statement Monday. “We take allegations very seriously and pray for everyone affected during this challenging time.”

It was not immediately clear whether Tyler Boebert has a lawyer to speak on his behalf. An attorney who previously represented him in a separate case did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The charges are linked to a 2024 video Tyler Boebert allegedly recorded with a 17-year-old, according to an affidavit in support of an arrest warrant. He was 18 at the time.

The 17-year-old’s mother later alerted authorities that a video showing her daughter and Tyler Boebert having sex was posted on Instagram, the affidavit says. The affidavit does not say who is alleged to have posted the video.
Tyler Boebert was charged with three counts of sexual exploitation of a child and two counts of contributing to the delinquency of a minor, court records show.
He was previously arrested on charges police described as a string of vehicle trespass and property thefts.
That case continues, according to Colorado Public Radio.
After her son was arrested in 2024, Lauren Boebert said he had been through “some very difficult, public challenges for a young man and the subject of attention that he didn’t ask for.”

“It breaks my heart to see my child struggling and, in this situation, especially when he has been provided multiple opportunities to get his life on track,” she said. “I will never give up on him, and I will continue to be there for him.”

title: Recount puts Trump-backed challenger in the lead in Indiana state Senate primary
summary: State Sen. Spencer Deery, who now trails Republican Paula Copenhaver by three votes, said he will appeal.
story: A recount in a contested Indiana state Senate primary in May has put Republican Paula Copenhaver, who was backed by President Donald Trump, ahead of incumbent Spencer Deery.

Deery was one of seven GOP members of the state Senate who faced primary challengers this spring after having voted down a redrawn congressional map that Trump pushed last year. Five lost, while Deery clung to a three-vote lead, which Copenhaver challenged.
On Monday, the Indiana Recount Commission threw out 10 votes — eight for Deery and two for Copenhaver — the Indiana Capital Chronicle reported, giving Copenhaver a three-vote edge.

Deery said on X that he would appeal the decision, calling it an “attempt to undermine the will of voters by treating ballots differently based on whether they furthered the president’s political goals.”
In a text message to NBC News, Deery said the commission’s ruling set a bad precedent for future election challenges.

“What was most remarkable about today’s hearing was that voter intent was never in question. None of the ballots challenged were discarded because there was uncertainty about whom the voter intended to support. The disputes instead centered on technicalities resulting from errors by government officials,” he said. “We are confident Indiana’s appellate courts will restore the vote totals that have been counted and recounted and reaffirm the choice voters made in Senate District 23.”
Copenhaver, an aide to Lt. Gov. Micah Beckwith, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

If her victory survives appeal, Copenhaver would be favored in the general election in the heavily Republican 23rd State Senate District. West Lafayette City Council member David Sanders, a Democrat, and independent Joshua Brant are also running.

The new state Senate could reconsider redistricting ahead of the 2028 election. Senate President Rod Bray, who also opposed the Trump-backed map, said last month that he would not seek another term as Republican leader.
Trump celebrated his announcement on Truth Social.

“I want to thank the Great State of Indiana for your support, not only in my Presidential Election, which we won with the Highest Vote in the History of the State, but also for your support in getting rid of wayward Senators, led down the Path of Destruction by a FOOL named Rodric Bray,” he wrote.

title: West Nile virus season peaks in late August — here’s what you can use to stay safe
summary: West Nile virus cases typically peak in late summer. Here’s how it spreads, the symptoms to watch for and expert-backed tips to avoid mosquito bites.
story: Summer isn’t over yet — and neither is mosquito season, which means you still have a very real chance of catching West Nile virus. In fact, every year, cases of this virus typically peak in late August to early September, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). And the rise in cases has already started — in recent weeks, cases have been reported in 24 states, according to the CDC’s tracking website.

“Early data on weather patterns (and surveillance data suggest we may see the highest infection numbers [of West Nile virus] since the early 2000s,” says Dr. Jagdish Khubchandani, a professor of public health at New Mexico State University.

West Nile virus is most commonly spread to people through bites from an infected mosquito. And while Cleveland Clinic reports that most people who get infected don’t develop any symptoms, some do experience a mild, flu-like illness, while a smaller percentage can develop severe illness that requires hospitalization. With no vaccine or specific treatment available, prevention is key.

Below, we break down what you need to know about West Nile virus — including the symptoms to watch for and the best products on the market to protect yourself and your family from mosquito bites this season.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
What is West Nile virus and how do you get it?

West Nile virus is most commonly spread to people through the bite of an infected mosquito. Research from the American Society of Microbiology states that mosquitoes pick up the virus after feeding on infected birds, then pass it along to people (and other animals) through subsequent bites. Each year, about 2,000 people in the U.S. are diagnosed with West Nile virus, though this is likely an undercount, since most people who get infected never develop symptoms or attribute mild ones to something else, according to the CDC. Mosquito season generally runs from June through October, with West Nile cases typically peaking in late August to early September.

While a mosquito bite is by far the most common way people get infected, it’s not the only one: In rare cases, West Nile virus can also spread through blood transfusions and organ transplants or from a mother to a baby during pregnancy, delivery or breastfeeding, according to Cleveland Clinic.
What are the symptoms of West Nile virus?

Most people who get infected with West Nile virus don’t develop any symptoms at all. But the CDC reports that about 20 percent of people will experience a fever along with other flu-like symptoms, sometimes referred to as West Nile fever. Symptoms typically show up two to six days after a bite, though it can take as long as 14 days before someone begins to feel ill. In rare cases — in less than 1 percent, to be exact — the virus can affect the brain or spinal cord, leading to more serious complications like encephalitis or meningitis.
The Mayo Clinic reports that the most common symptoms of West Nile virus include:
Fever Headache Muscle achesNausea and vomitingDiarrheaRash, usually concentrated around the chest and back Swollen lymph nodesSore throat Pain behind the eyes

Why does West Nile virus peak in August?

The timing comes down to biology. According to research published in the Journal of Medical Entomology, warm summer temperatures speed up mosquito larvae development, which drives mosquito populations up through the early and midsummer months. At the same time birds are laying and hatching lots of eggs and nestlings and fledglings create prime ways for mosquitoes to pick up the virus, according to Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.

By the time case counts rise in July and peak in August, with a plateau into September, mosquito populations are at their most active and infectious — before the cooler weather in October causes both mosquito activity and case numbers to drop off. In other words, late summer is the window when infected mosquitoes, warm weather and human outdoor activity all overlap, making it the riskiest stretch of the year for exposure.
The best products for reducing the risk of West Nile virus

The best defense against West Nile is simply avoiding mosquito bites in the first place. That means taking preventive measures to avoid getting bitten. “First, remember the peak activity times of mosquitoes — early morning and early evenings — and try to avoid going out at these times,” says professor Khubchandani. “Second, use quality insect repellants, especially during these times.” Khubchandani also suggests staying vigilant about your outdoor spaces — if you see a lot of mosquitoes around you, look to address the issue with products like mosquito dunks (more on those below).

Below, I’ve rounded up a few mosquito repellent products — including repellents and other items that will help you manage mosquitoes in your space — that experts have previously recommended to NBC Selected as good ways to ward off mosquitoes.
Summit Mosquito Dunks

Experts previously recommended these mosquito dunks as an effective way to prevent mosquitoes from taking over your home. Mosquito dunks are small round rings that you put in water — think ponds, bird baths and any other body of standing water. They work by releasing natural bacteria into the water. When mosquito larvae hatch, they eat the floating bacteria and the toxins kill them within 48 hours, according to the brand. Also helpful to know: These dunks aren’t toxic to other animals and they last for 30 days.
Thermacell Rechargeable Mosquito Repeller

This device essentially builds an invisible barrier around a small area to keep mosquitoes away. It’s rechargeable and disperses a repellent that works within a 20-foot radius, according to the brand. The device comes with a USB-C charging cable and several repellent cartridges, each providing up to 12 hours of protection. My 1-year-old son reacts terribly to mosquito bites — I’m talking huge welts that blister and swell — so we have one of these on our front porch and another on the back porch and they keep our home free from the biting pests.
Gootop Indoor/Outdoor Bug Zapper

Gootop’s Outdoor Bug Zapper can be hung from a patio awning or set on a table, ledge, or other flat surface. It works by emitting a blue light that draws in flying insects, then zaps them once they get close, helping clear the area of flies, mosquitoes, gnats, wasps and more. According to the brand, a single unit can cover up to half an acre. Cleanup is simple, too: Dead bugs collect in a removable tray at the base, which can be wiped out with the included brush. The zapper has racked up nearly 20,000 five-star ratings, with reviewers praising how easy it is to hang and how effectively it clears insects from their space.
Ben's Tick & Insect Repellent Eco Spray

This unscented body repellent spray is designed to guard against ticks and mosquitoes using a 30 percent concentration of DEET, which experts have previously told us is the most effective ingredient in bug sprays for repelling mosquitoes. The formula is water-based rather than alcohol-based, which helps more of the product stay on the skin instead of evaporating during application, according to the brand. Its spray nozzle also releases a continuous mist, making it easy to cover exposed areas, including harder-to-reach spots like your back.
Sawyer Picaridin Insect Repellent

This repellent is formulated with 20 percent picaridin, a popular alternative to DEET that offers comparable effectiveness while typically feeling less greasy on skin and being gentler on fabrics. According to the company, this formula provides up to 12 hours of protection against mosquitoes and ticks, and eight hours against flies, gnats and chiggers. This is my go-to for my daughter, who goes to summer camp in the forest. I spray her down every morning and she’s never come home with a mosquito bite or tick.
Frequently asked questions

The vast majority of people infected with West Nile virus — roughly 80 percent, according to the CDC — never develop any symptoms at all. About one in five experience a mild, flu-like illness, while fewer than 1 percent go on to develop a serious infection affecting the brain or nervous system.
If symptoms do develop, they typically emerge two to 14 days after a bite from an infected mosquito, starting with sudden fever, headache, body aches and pronounced fatigue, according to the CDC.

If you develop symptoms like fever, headache or body aches after spending time outdoors, it’s worth checking in with a healthcare provider, especially if you know you’ve been bitten by mosquitoes recently. There’s no specific treatment for West Nile virus disease, so for mild illness, doctors typically recommend the same at-home care you’d use for a cold or flu — rest, fluids and pain medications to relieve symptoms, according to the CDC.

If you experience warning signs of more serious illness — think high fever, neck stiffness, muscle weakness, confusion or tremors — don’t wait it out at home. Head to the emergency room right away, since these can be signs that the virus has affected your brain or spinal cord and may require hospitalization, advises the CDC.

title: You won’t want to wait until winter to return these recalled handwarmers — here’s why
summary: Ocoopa has recalled 1.5 million rechargeable hand warmers after reports of fires, burns and one death. Here’s what happened, how to check your device and safer alternatives.
story: While your stash of hand warmers is likely not top of mind while the summer sun is still heating up your days , a recent recall is worth paying attention to. Ocoopa has recalled 1.5 million rechargeable hand warmers across seven models after the lithium-ion batteries inside were found to overheat and ignite, posing a risk of serious injury or death from fire and burn hazards. The company has received reports of 15 fires and 350 burn injuries, including the death of an 83-year-old consumer in California.

Below, we’ve broken down everything you need to know about this recall, what to do if you have any of the recalled models, and how to recoup your money — plus, we offer some alternatives that you can shop right now, before the cold season returns.
Why were Ocoopa hand warmers recalled?

On July 30, the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) published an announcement explaining that Ocoopa Direct had issued a recall of its rechargeable hand warmers. The lithium-ion batteries inside the recalled devices can overheat and ignite when in use or while charging, posing a risk of serious injury or death from fire and burn hazards.

Ocoopa Direct has received 1,480 reports of hand warmers overheating, resulting in 15 fires and 350 burn injuries. Among those injuries was the death of an 83-year-old consumer in San José, California in February 2026. The recalled hand warmers were sold online at Amazon, Walmart, ocoopa.com and ocoopa.net from September 2018 through May 2026 and cost between $15 and $60.

The recall covers Ocoopa-branded rechargeable hand warmers under the model numbers UT3053, UT3056, ZLS-118, ZLS-118S, ZLS-118D, H01 and H01(PD). The dual-sided hand warmers were sold in a variety of colors and designs, in packs of two that can be joined magnetically, along with a charging cable. Each unit has a USB-C charging port, adjustable heat settings, LED indicator lights and a silicone lanyard, with “OCOOPA” printed on top. The model number and a three-digit batch number are printed on the underside of each hand warmer. You can check this to see if you have a recalled model so that you can now.
What to do if you have the recalled hand warmers

If you have any of the recalled hand warmers, you should stop using them immediately. Consumers are asked to write “RECALLED” on the device in permanent marker and submit a photo of that marking, along with the model number and batch number, to Ocoopa’s product recall page in order to receive a full refund via gift card or original payment method. Because the devices contain lithium-ion batteries, they should not be thrown in the trash or regular recycling bins — and they should not be mailed back to the company. Instead, they need to be taken to a household hazardous waste collection center.

You can check your local city or county public works department to find your closest hazardous waste collection center, or go to the United States Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) site to search for a hazardous waste management facility in your area. It’s advised that you call to ensure that the center will accept defective lithium-ion batteries before you take them there.

It’s also best to return the recalled hand warmers as soon as possible and not wait until winter. For one, by the time you need them you may forget about the recall and plug them in or use them, which increases your risk or hazard. Additionally, you’ll need to replace them once it’s really cold outside and if you wait until you need them to replace them, you may be tempted to use the warmers despite the defective batteries. In order to ensure your safety and the safety of your family and home, do not take the gamble and use recalled hand warmers.
Alternatives to rechargeable hand warmers
HotHands Toe, Hand, & Body Warmer Variety Pack

If you’re worried about a lithium battery, consider this variety pack of disposable warmers. The pack includes five pairs of hand warmers, five super warmers and three pairs of toe warmers — no batteries required. Each single-use, air-activated warmer heats up within minutes and lasts for hours, offering a no-charge, no-fire-risk alternative to rechargeable warmers.
HotHands Glove Warmers

HotHands Glove Warmers are stretchy, one-size-fits-most liners you layer under your own gloves, each with a built-in pocket to keep HotHands Hand Warmers close to your hands. They’re washable and reusable, and compact enough to slip into a backpack or purse. This pack comes with a free pair of hand warmers.
Rivmount Waterproof Fleece Gloves

If you’d rather skip hand warmers altogether, a genuinely good pair of insulated, windproof and waterproof gloves like these can keep your hands warm on their own. They have a soft fleece lining and adjustable cuffs to lock out cold and snow. They also have touchscreen-compatible fingertips that let you use your phone without needing to take the gloves off.

title: The U.S. just had its hottest month on record
summary: NOAA’s report said last month was not only the warmest July but also the warmest month in the agency’s 132 years of record-keeping.
story: The United States sweltered through its hottest July ever recorded last month, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration confirmed Monday.

Warmer-than-normal temperatures affected the entire contiguous U.S., averaging 76.9 degrees for the month, which was 3.3 degrees above the 20th-century average, according to NOAA. The troubling milestone came amid a month chock-full of extreme weather events that hit nearly every corner of the country, including heat waves, drought, severe storms, flooding and wildfires.
NOAA’s report said July 2026 was not only the warmest July but also the warmest month in the agency’s 132 years of record-keeping.

title: Police question person of interest after Mississippi woman found hanging from tree
summary: A 29-year-old Black woman from Mississippi was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home in Jackson last week.
story: A 29-year-old Black woman from Mississippi was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home in Jackson last week.
The body was discovered Aug. 3 in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance, the Jackson Police Department said in a statement.
The Hinds County Coroner’s Office identified the woman as Tasia Fortune. Police said the circumstances surrounding her death remain under investigation.
“This is an active and ongoing investigation,” the police department said. “We will provide updates as new details develop.”
Terence Anderson, 65, who is said to be a person of interest in connection with Fortune’s death, was taken into custody on an unrelated weapons charge, NBC affiliate WLBT of Jackson reported.
Anderson’s brother, Tony Anderson, confirmed the arrest to NBC News. He said Fortune and his brother have a 5-year-old son together and that the child lived with Terence.
He also said he does not think his brother was involved in Fortune’s death.

“Sometimes they’ll have a few occasions where they may get into it or whatever, but that was about it,” Tony Anderson said. “They had their good days, their bad days, but I don’t think he done nothing like that. The autopsy will tell actually what happened to her.”
Christy Spivey, Fortune’s mother, told ABC News that she last saw her daughter July 26 at a family reunion in Kentucky.
“This has just devastated us,” she said, remembering her daughter as someone who “was strong-minded” and “full of laughs and love.”
Spivey said that the last time she saw her daughter she seemed to be in good spirits.
“She was better than I had seen her in a long time,” she told the station. “She was at peace.”
Spivey said she does not believe Fortune died by suicide.
“She did not do this to herself,” she said. “I know my daughter and she did not do this to herself.”
Spivey could not immediately be reached for comment Monday. The State Medical Examiner’s Office said it will conduct an autopsy and release its findings once the investigation is complete.
Fortune’s death has left some people searching for answers.
Ward 3 City Council member Kenneth Stokes said in a letter to U.S. Attorney Baxter Kruger that the city was in “dire need of assistance” while the case is investigated, WLBT reported.
During a recent court appearance, detectives said Terence Anderson had been interviewed about Fortune’s death, the news station reported.
He denied any involvement but told police that he had an argument with Fortune, according to WLBT.

Tony Anderson told NBC News his brother is a convicted felon but had been out of trouble for years and has a job working as a painter. “He pretty much looked after his little boy and worked,” he said.
Tony also said Fortune had a substance abuse problem and was living at the abandoned home where her body was found.
Jackson police did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 or go to 988lifeline.org to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Mark Zuckerberg’s mega-yacht didn’t respond to call for help from small boat in Alaska
summary: When the captain of the boat that did respond announced Zuckerberg’s cruiser was closer and hadn’t answered the call, “there was near unanimous booing,” a passenger said.
story: Meta billionaire Mark Zuckerberg is the owner of a two-year-old mega-yacht called Launchpad that is 387 feet long, has a steel hull and is propelled by four engines capable of generating 5,846 horsepower apiece.

But when a small skiff was in trouble off Alaska last week in the same waters as Zuckerberg’s vessel, it was a 42-year-old tour boat called Wilderness Legacy that steamed to the rescue, according to the Coast Guard.

And when the captain of the tour boat announced Zuckerberg’s cutting-edge cruiser, which cost between $300 million and $390 million to construct, had been closer to the stricken skiff and hadn’t answered the radio call for help, “there was near unanimous booing,” passenger Michael Love posted on Bluesky.
The Coast Guard got a call for help just after 9:30 p.m. on Aug. 3 after a 21-foot skiff ran out of fuel between Petersburg and Juneau, the Coast Guard said in a statement to the Alaska Beacon.
“At approximately 9:56 p.m., the Coast Guard determined they were not in distress and issued a marine assistance request broadcast on their behalf,” the statement said.
The Wilderness Legacy, which was completed in 1984 and is a replica of turn-of-the-century coastal steamers complete with Victorian-style wood cabinetry, was the first to respond.
It scooted around the Launchpad and towed the stranded skiff back to the safety of Farragut Bay, the news outlet reported.
The local story went viral after Love, a software developer from New York City, posted about the incident on Bluesky.

“I’m on a small-ship Alaska cruise with my son; our boat rescued a stranded vessel last night and apparently we did that after the Coast Guard radioed Mark Zuckerberg’s yacht — which was closer — and they repeatedly refused to respond,” he wrote.
Zuckerberg spokesperson Brian Baker said the skiff was already in the process of being rescued when the Launchpad crew learned it was in trouble.

“As the Coast Guard noted, the boat was not in distress, and by the time the crew reviewed the Coast Guard contact on a different radio channel from the one they were operating on, the assist was already underway,” Baker said.
“We’re grateful all parties are safe,” he said.
Baker added that neither Zuckerberg nor his family were aboard the Launchpad at the time.

The International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, or SOLAS, which is an international treaty that was first adopted in 1914 in response to the Titanic disaster, lays out what’s been called “one of the oldest duties in maritime law.”

“The master of a ship at sea, on receiving a signal from any source that a ship or aircraft or survival craft thereof is in distress, is bound to proceed with all speed to the assistance of the persons in distress informing them if possible that he is doing so,” it says.

title: Slain Arizona student planned to break up with her Indian boyfriend, arrest warrant says
summary: Julissa Rubi Salazar feared for her safety and decided to end the relationship, her roommate told police after the 19-year-old was found dead in her bed.
story: The University of Arizona student who was killed in her Tucson apartment planned to break up with her Indian boyfriend and feared for her safety in the relationship, according to findings in an arrest warrant filed with the court in Pima County.

Julissa Rubi Salazar, 19, discussed ending her relationship with Varun Batchigari, 20, according to a roommate who provided details to police after the young woman’s body was found Thursday in her bed, fully clothed and covered by a blanket.

The victim told her roommate that Batchigari was abusive and had sexually assaulted and choked her in the past after an altercation at a Halloween party, according to an arrest warrant affidavit. That roommate conveyed that the sexual assault was not reported to the police.
Batchigari has an open misdemeanor assault case from May. The circumstances of the matter were not immediately available in public records, and it is unclear whether it involved Salazar.

Salazar’s body had injuries that suggested she was strangled, including redness and scratches around her neck, along with petechiae marks on her eyes, eyelids and face that indicate trauma from popped blood vessels, the affidavit said. There were also injuries consistent with defensive wounds on the victim, according to an investigative narrative in the warrant.
Investigators found Salazar’s room in disarray with broken glass and a knocked-over plant, indicating signs of struggle. Police could not find Salazar’s keys and phone.
Federal and international authorities helped to facilitate Batchigari’s arrest in Germany last week during his multileg trip from Tucson to India.
Batchigari, who is charged with first-degree murder and kidnapping, is awaiting extradition back to Arizona.

The affidavit also states that Salazar’s phone pinged at the Tucson International Airport on Thursday morning, about an hour before Batchigari took a flight to Houston, where he had a layover on his way to Europe.

The young woman had planned to visit her mother in Yuma, Arizona, but canceled the visit via text. Her mother told police that the text struck her as odd. Her mother thought “something was off with the messages,” the document said.

On Wednesday, Salazar’s mother was able to see her location through the location-sharing function on her daughter’s phone. By the following day, the feature had been disabled, according to the warrant papers.
Salazar, who was also known as Julie, was a student in the university’s elite science, engineering and math program. The apartment where she was killed was near the University of Arizona.
Another roommate who spoke to police told them there was “loud screaming and yelling” and “another brief outburst” before silence in the apartment Wednesday, the day before Salazar’s body was found.
Salazar was named “mentor of the month” in her program in March, with the school posting a complimentary blurb about her on its official Instagram account.

“We are recognizing Julie for her intentionality in building rapport with students, connecting with each of them personally and providing individualized support of each of her students,” the post read. “Her positive attitude and bubbly demeanor is a wonderful addition to our team!”
A GoFundMe page was started for Salazar’s family to pay for funeral costs and other expenses.

“It is with unimaginable sadness that we share the unexpected passing of Julie, a beautiful 19-year-old daughter, sister, friend, and beloved member of her family,” a statement on the site read. “Julie was loved deeply, and she will be missed beyond measure.”

If you or someone you know is facing domestic violence, call the National Domestic Violence hotline for help at (800) 799-SAFE (7233) or go to www.thehotline.org for more. States often have domestic violence hotlines, as well.

title: Recount puts Trump-backed challenger in the lead in Indiana state Senate primary
summary: State Sen. Spencer Deery, who now trails Republican Paula Copenhaver by three votes, said he will appeal.
story: A recount in a contested Indiana state Senate primary in May has put Republican Paula Copenhaver, who was backed by President Donald Trump, ahead of incumbent Spencer Deery.

Deery was one of seven GOP members of the state Senate who faced primary challengers this spring after having voted down a redrawn congressional map that Trump pushed last year. Five lost, while Deery clung to a three-vote lead, which Copenhaver challenged.
On Monday, the Indiana Recount Commission threw out 10 votes — eight for Deery and two for Copenhaver — the Indiana Capital Chronicle reported, giving Copenhaver a three-vote edge.

Deery said on X that he would appeal the decision, calling it an “attempt to undermine the will of voters by treating ballots differently based on whether they furthered the president’s political goals.”
In a text message to NBC News, Deery said the commission’s ruling set a bad precedent for future election challenges.

“What was most remarkable about today’s hearing was that voter intent was never in question. None of the ballots challenged were discarded because there was uncertainty about whom the voter intended to support. The disputes instead centered on technicalities resulting from errors by government officials,” he said. “We are confident Indiana’s appellate courts will restore the vote totals that have been counted and recounted and reaffirm the choice voters made in Senate District 23.”
Copenhaver, an aide to Lt. Gov. Micah Beckwith, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

If her victory survives appeal, Copenhaver would be favored in the general election in the heavily Republican 23rd State Senate District. West Lafayette City Council member David Sanders, a Democrat, and independent Joshua Brant are also running.

The new state Senate could reconsider redistricting ahead of the 2028 election. Senate President Rod Bray, who also opposed the Trump-backed map, said last month that he would not seek another term as Republican leader.
Trump celebrated his announcement on Truth Social.

“I want to thank the Great State of Indiana for your support, not only in my Presidential Election, which we won with the Highest Vote in the History of the State, but also for your support in getting rid of wayward Senators, led down the Path of Destruction by a FOOL named Rodric Bray,” he wrote.

title: Jennifer Balkcom picked to replace Rep. Chuck Edwards in N.C. congressional race
summary: Edwards dropped his re-election bid after the House Ethics Committee recommended he be censured over sexual harassment allegations. He has denied any wrongdoing.
story: A panel of Republican officials in North Carolina selected a state lawmaker Monday as the GOP nominee in a House race after embattled Rep. Chuck Edwards dropped his re-election bid following sexual harassment allegations.
Jennifer Balkcom, who represents a state legislative district in Henderson County, will face Jamie Ager, who won the Democratic primary in March.
The North Carolina GOP’s Executive Committee for the 11th Congressional District picked Balkcom to replace Edwards in compliance with state law given how late in the campaign he dropped out.
Balkcom faces a sprint to Election Day, which is less than three months away. Absentee ballots are set to start going out Sept. 4, giving her just a few weeks to make her case to some voters.
She announced her intention to seek the nomination less than 24 hours ago.

“This race is too important to sit out,” Balkcom wrote in a statement Sunday on X, adding that Western North Carolina “needs a strong voice right now” as it continues to rebuild after Hurricane Helene.

Balkcom’s candidacy was heavily boosted by power players in the state. North Carolina House Speaker Destin Hall, a Republican, endorsed her on social media Monday afternoon, calling her “the right person at the right time.”
“Jennifer is a principled conservative, a tireless advocate for her district, and a leader who gets things done,” Hall wrote on X.

The state GOP’s executive director, Zachary Almond, congratulated Balkcom on X after her nomination was announced, saying he was “excited to work alongside her and her team throughout the election cycle.”

Edwards, who had been endorsed by President Donald Trump, announced last week that he would serve out his term in Congress but would not seek a third term in the House. His decision came days after the House Ethics Committee recommended a censure following a probe that found “substantial reason to believe Representative Edwards violated House Rules related to sexual harassment and hostile workplaces.”

He has repeatedly denied wrongdoing, and the Ethics Committee said Edwards, who cooperated with the panel’s investigation, had denied that any of his actions were meant to be sexual or romantic in nature. Attorneys for Edwards wrote a 15-page response to the committee’s findings, calling them “unfounded.”
Edwards previously called the allegations “baseless,” and in May he said he welcomed an investigation.

Edwards was elected to the House in 2022 after having ousted the scandal-ridden Rep. Madison Cawthorn in the GOP primary. Before that, the district was represented by Mark Meadows, who led the House Freedom Caucus before he stepped down to become White House chief of staff during Trump’s first term.

Edwards won his seat by more than 13 percentage points in 2024, but Democrats are hopeful they can flip it as Republicans seek to defend their narrow majority in the House heading into the midterm elections.

Ager, a farmer who significantly outraised Edwards in the race, was previously listed as “Likely Republican” by the nonpartisan Cook Political Report. The rating was downgraded to “Lean Republican” before the House Ethics Committee report was released.

title: Usher Responds to Rumors as Fans Believe He’s Hired a Look-Alike to Perform at Concerts
summary: Usher is shutting down rumors that he’s been sending out an imposter to perform in his place during his recent joint tour with Chris Brown.
story: Usher is shutting down rumors that he’s been sending out an imposter to perform in his place during his recent joint tour with Chris Brown.
Fans have been doing double takes for days after footage from a recent “The R&B Tour” concert has convinced many of them that the man performing on stage was a fake.

Sunnya Sultan, who saw the tour in person Aug. 7 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, shared a TikTok video questioning if the 47-year-old “Yeah” singer was truly the one dancing in front of her.
The performer wears a white with lime green and pink ensemble, ball cap and sunglasses as he sings and dances.
Sultan tells TODAY.com she believes she did see Usher perform. She’s also convinced an Usher look-alike also took the stage during a portion of the show.

“Usher came out. The real Usher came out but then he sang like half a song, maybe for like 40 seconds,” Sultan recalls. “Then he goes into this darkness and he comes out, and as he’s walking, I think everyone really thought that was Usher.”
“But as the first song finishes, I think everyone started getting confused because the way he was moving wasn’t really Usher,” she continues.

When she looked closely, she believed something was off about the Usher who now appeared onstage. She noted that his jawline that was “a little too chiseled” and the performer “seemed a little too stiff.”
Also, he was dressed differently. The “real” Usher, she says, came out shirtless and wearing a fur coat.
The Usher who later performed in front of her, she adds, was “fully covered,” as seen in her TikTok video.
“Everything was just kind of weird,” Sultan says. “He looked like him, and then at certain angles he definitely did not look like him.”
Sultan said concertgoers all around her were suspicious.
Usher addressed the rumors in a video posted on the tour’s official Instagram Aug. 9.
“Usure? Wesure,” reads the caption.
The video showed Usher performing onstage in the same white ensemble. It also included screenshots of Usher replying to comments made about the alleged imposter.
“Ya’ll are funny…clone? They can’t clone this??” the singer wrote alongside a laughing emoji.
“How ya’ll come up with this? AI ain’t that advanced,” he added along with more laughing emoji.

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Has Shocking Elimination After Dancer Failed to Deliver ‘Wow Moment’
summary: Who was eliminated on ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ episode 5? The Aug. 10 episode saw a shocking elimination after one dancer failed to deliver a “wow moment.”
story: The competition continues on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” and now it’s time to shine.
In the Aug. 10 episode of the “Dancing With the Stars” spinoff, pro Daniella Karagach showed off her impressive skills with a mega performance as host Robert Irwin introduced the challenge.

This week it was all about having that “wow” moment that “DWTS” viewers love. The six remaining dancers were mentored and guided by Daniella as they created a contemporary routine that incorporated one of her signature and viral moves.
If the dancers failed to deliver a spectacular move in their choreographer, they would be at risk for elimination. But first, the contestants took a trip to the Australia Zoo for inspiration.
What Happened During Episode 5 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’

When Daniella entered the rehearsal room, she told the dancers that they also had to create their own standout moment that would “forever be embedded in someone’s memory.” This was in addition to including one of Daniella’s “wow” moves.
“The more you wow the audience, the longer you and your partner stay in the competition,” she said about competing on “DWTS.”

Since last week, the ladies got to choose their partners, this week the guys picked who they wanted to perform with. If more than one guy chose the same girl, she would have the option to choose who she wanted to partner up with.
Allen Genkin chose Adele Zaikman, while AJ Pritchard and Erik Linder chose Selena Hamilton. No one chose Nina Mayster.
Selena ultimately chose Erik, meaning AJ and Nina would be partners by default.

AJ and Nina were up first, performing a contemporary piece to “Human” by Christina Perri that impressed the judges. Daniella told them they “understood the assignment,” while judge Mark Ballas complimented their “total trust.”
Shirley Ballas also applauded their multiple wow moments, AJ’s vulnerability and Nina’s musicality.
Next were Allen and Adele, who also got major kudos from the judges with their routine to “All That Really Matters” by Illenium featuring Teddy Swims.
Mark was a fan of their wow moments, that included the Allen-copter and caveman walk at the beginning. He also called Adele a “diamond.”
Shirley echoed her son’s comments, calling her “beyond a diamond, one of the best female dancers I’ve ever seen.” Daniella also shared how she loved the routine.
Last but not least were Erik and Selena, who specializes in contemporary, with a routine to “You Stole the Show” by Sienna Spiro.
Shirley began her comments by saying she was “conflicted” and didn’t know what their wow moment was. Selena replied that sometimes the “wow” is in the silence.
Shirley continued by saying she would have liked to see Erik let go more and ultimately wasn’t impressed. While she did appreciate the quality of Selena’s routine, she expected more.
Mark and Daniella both shared kind words about their dancing, but noted that they did not follow direction.
Who Was in the Bottom 2?
Because they did not complete the challenge and include a visibly “wow moment” in their routine, Erik and Selena were on the chopping block.
The other four contestants were visibly emotional in the background, as Daniella said, “If you have a challenge, you have to deliver it. You have to make that the priority.”
Who Got Eliminated on Episode 5 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?
Ultimately, Shirley shared that with a “very, very heavy heart” this would be the last dance for Erik.
Allen broke down in tears, with Adele and Nina covering their faces in shock.
Shirley told Erik that he was “a beautiful dancer,” but applauded Selena for her strong and advanced choreography.

“I knew that I was taking a risk,” Erik said in his confessional, adding that he didn’t regret a single decision that he made. He then thanked the judges for the opportunity to grow as a dancer and person.
What Will Happen Next Week?
Five dancers remain on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.” For the Aug. 17 episode, guest judge Witney Carson will deliver the dancers’ toughest challenge yet: teaching ballroom novice.
In the next episode, the contestants will be paired with “DWTS” superfans who are dancing amateurs. They will then have two days to prepare a performance that will land them a spot in the semifinals.

title: Brad Pitt Makes Rare Comment About ‘Pain’ of ‘Family Stuff’
summary: In a new interview, Brad Pitt shares that he’s never been suicidal “except for one little period” that was related to “family stuff.”
story: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. You can also text HOME to 741741 or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional resources.
In a rare mention of his personal life, Brad Pitt says in a new interview that he has never been suicidal “except for one little period” that was related to “family stuff.”

The 62-year-old Hollywood icon made a short reference to his family situation in an interview with Esquire published on Aug. 10  in which he talked about “oppressive” pain that led him to a dark place where he could “understand suicide.”
In the Esquire interview, Pitt initially shared his thoughts about going to dark places in life, unconnected to any question about his family.
“I was never suicidal in any way,” he said. “It just was not my makeup. In fact, if I have any afflictions, it’s probably being a congenital optimist,” he said.
He reiterated he’s “never been suicidal,” before adding, “except for one little period.”

“And in that one little period, I just thought — I just couldn’t — just didn’t see a way out,” he said. “The pain was so oppressive that — I wasn’t going to act on this, but I could feel — I could feel the cold steel of the bullet in my head, and it felt like relief. And I thought, Oh, okay, now I understand — I understand suicide, in the sense that it’s just relief. It’s just looking for relief from the pain. But I also think we have incredible survival instincts. And for me, that immediately kicked in, but it was just ...”
Pitt was asked what could have provoked him to think about suicide in that way. The reporter questioned if it was “kid stuff,” per the Esquire article.
“Family stuff,” Pitt said. “We could leave it at that.”

Pitt and his ex-wife, Angelina Jolie, have six children. The couple reached a divorce settlement in 2024 after Jolie accused Pitt of verbal and physical abuse, which he has denied. Their daughter Shiloh, 20, legally dropped “Pitt” from her last name when she turned 18 in 2024. Two of his other children have also considered ditching “Pitt” from their last name, according to a court filing in California cited by CNN in July 2026.
The “F1” star was later asked how he endured the difficult period he referenced.

“I don’t see it as climbing out of it,” he said. “It’s going through it and trying and trying and trying and trying to the point of exhaustion and then trying again. I don’t want to ignore the place where you run up against the wall. But I just one day woke up, and it just felt a little sunnier and the air felt a little sweeter. Just microdoses of it.”

Pitt does not make it clear in the interview what “little period” he is referring to in his life. Elsewhere in the interview, he discussed the death of his mother in August 2025 and said, referencing his father, “Let’s just say it’s better to be the one who goes first.”
Once Hollywood’s most famous couple, Pitt, and Jolie, 51, met on the set of the 2005 movie “Mr. & Mrs. Smith” and got married in 2014. Jolie filed for divorce in 2016.

In 2022, amid already contentious divorce proceedings, Jolie accused Pitt of physical and verbal abuse on a 2016 flight from France to Los Angeles, during which he allegedly choked one of their children, which prompted her to file for divorce, according to a court filing from Jolie.
“Brad has owned everything he’s responsible for from day one — unlike the other side — but he’s not going to own anything he didn’t do,” a lawyer for Pitt said in 2022.

No criminal charges were ever filed against Pitt. In 2016, both the FBI and the Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services closed an investigation into allegations of abuse onboard the flight.

The acrimony since their split has also included Pitt filing a lawsuit in 2022 accusing Jolie of intentionally harming him and the French winery business they once shared by selling her stake in it. The former couple purchased shares in the 148-acre French vineyard Chateau Miraval together in 2008.

Following Pitt’s lawsuit about the winery, Jolie filed the 2022 cross-complaint that alleged Pitt subjected their family to verbal and physical abuse aboard the aforementioned 2016 flight from France to Los Angeles.
Their divorce was settled in 2024, and the dispute over the winery remains ongoing.

title: Romy Reiner’s Latest TV Role Has a Touching Tie to Her Late Dad, Rob Reiner
summary: Romy Reiner appeared in the finale of Larry David’s “Life, Larry, and the Pursuit of Unhappiness,” which her dad Rob Reiner also appeared in.
story: Romy Reiner followed in her late father Rob Reiner’s footsteps by appearing on Larry David’s “Life, Larry, and the Pursuit of Unhappiness.”
The elder Reiner made a posthumous cameo in the sketch show in an episode that aired July 3, months after his shocking death. He played George Washington.
Romy Reiner, meanwhile, guest-starred in the series finale on Aug. 7 as a nurse caring for President William Henry Harrison (Fred Melamed).
Romy Reiner’s appearance comes five years after she got her big break in 2021 playing a cashier on David’s HBO series “Curb Your Enthusiasm.” David was one of Rob Reiner’s close friends.
The 28-year-old actor is the youngest child of the legendary actor and director and his late wife Michele Singer.
The couple, who were married for 36 years, were found fatally stabbed at home on Dec. 14, 2025, according to the L.A. district attorney’s office.
Their youngest son, Nick Reiner, 32, was arrested and charged Dec. 16 with two counts of first degree murder. In February, Nick Reiner pleaded not guilty to the charges.
The Reiners also shared an older son, Jake Reiner, 35, who posted a heartbreaking tribute to his parents in an April 24 post on Substack.
Rob Reiner was also the father of an adoptive daughter, Tracy Reiner, with his ex-wife, actor and director Penny Marshall.
In his essay on Substack, Jake Reiner revealed he was at a friend’s celebration of life in Los Angeles when his sister called to tell him their parents were dead.

“The 45-minute Lyft ride from downtown to the west side was unendurable,” he wrote. “My world, as I knew it, had collapsed. I was in a trance. The only thing I could focus on was that I needed to get to my childhood home. I needed to get to my sister. I needed to figure out what the hell just happened.”
Jake Reiner wrote about his grief that his parents won’t be alive to witness future milestones in his life.

“My parents won’t be at my wedding, they won’t get to hold their future grandchild, and they won’t get to see me have the successful career I’m still seeking,” he wrote. “It simultaneously breaks my heart and enrages me.”
Rob Reiner, who was 78 when he died, was the son of comedy legend Carl Reiner. He found fame in the early 1970s playing Michael “Meathead” Stivic on the sitcom “All in the Family.”

He went on to become one of Hollywood’s most beloved directors, helming the cult classic “This Is Spinal Tap” as well as the box office hits “Stand By Me,” “The Princess Bride,” “When Harry Met Sally,” “Misery” and “A Few Good Men.”
He married photographer and producer Michele Reiner in May 1989.
In his essay, Jake Reiner called his parents “the most giving people.” He described his father as his “hero” and Singer as “the backbone” of the family.
Losing his parents together in such a violent manner — with his brother “at the center of it” — has been, he wrote, a “living nightmare.”

title: New Yorker Accidentally Threw Away 2 Family Rings. 20,000 Pounds of Trash Later, They Were Recovered
summary: New York City sanitation workers dug through 20,000 pounds of garbage to ensure that one man’s trash didn’t also mean the loss of his treasure.
story: New York City sanitation workers dug through 20,000 pounds of garbage to ensure that one man’s trash didn’t also mean the loss of his treasure.
A Brooklyn man is breathing a massive sigh of relief after he accidentally threw a pair of priceless family rings in the garbage at a large residential building last month.

The ring’s owner realized the mistake before the trash was picked up, so he met sanitation workers at the curb on July 28 to explain the predicament, a spokesperson for the New York City Department of Sanitation told TODAY.com in an email statement.
The heirloom rings were a gold-and-diamond promise ring and platinum-and-diamond engagement ring that had been in the family for four generations, according to the DSNY.

Sanitation workers were able to isolate the truck and slowly dump the nearly 20,000 pounds of trash across a concrete floor to be searched. After only 10 minutes, the rings were found to the relief and joy of the resident, whose name was withheld by the DSNY.
“It isn’t exactly a needle in a haystack, but some accidentally discarded rings were dug up!,” the DSNY wrote on Facebook.
“Can you imagine?” Savannah Guthrie said on TODAY Aug. 10. “Out of the goodness of their hearts being like, ‘I’m going to sift through 20,000 pounds of trash,’ and they found it! Incredible.”
The DSNY spokesperson said searches like that happen multiple times a year, and there is a process for them.

Any residents who accidentally throw out a valuable item are urged to call 311 as soon as possible. After each call, sanitation workers aim to isolate the truck and slowly dump the contents on a concrete floor to be sifted through.

The timeliness of the call is crucial. If a truck has already dumped the trash at a transfer station, there’s no way to recover the lost item because it’s usually immediately mixed with trash from other trucks to be put into a barge or railcar.

The resident is allowed to participate in the search for his or her item and can bring one friend to help. The DSNY provides gloves, shovels, pickers and other tools for the search while also sharing possible spots to look. For instance, if the person’s address was at the beginning of the sanitation truck’s route, the material may be more near the back of the truck.
The recovery of the Brooklyn man’s rings is the latest success story for the DSNY, which has previously found everything from a wallet to a laptop that had been accidentally tossed out.
“Way to go New York City Sanitation,” Craig Melvin said on TODAY.

title: Anthony Bourdain’s Daughter Was A ‘Brutal’ Critic About His Cooking, He Joked In 2016 on TODAY
summary: In 2016, Anthony Bourdain sat down with TODAY’s Willie Geist to reflect on how he got into TV, his experiences traveling the world and cooking for his daughter.
story: Welcome inside the TODAY Vault, where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Anthony Bourdain’s conversation with Willie Geist on Oct. 23, 2016.
The legacy of Anthony Bourdain lives on with the release of “Tony,”
In the film, out now, Dominic Sessa plays the celebrated and complicated chef, who died in 2018 at the age of 61 by suicide, leaving behind a legion of fans who are still inspired by him.

In 2016, Bourdain sat down with Sunday TODAY’s Willie Geist to reflect on his career, remembering how he wound up a fixture of the small screen, what it was like to eat with the president and how his toughest critic may be his daughter.
How Did Anthony Bourdain Break Into Show Business?

Bourdain shot to stardom after he wrote the 2000 book “Kitchen Confidential,” which, based on his experience, took readers behind the scenes of the restaurant industry. It also touched on his personal struggles with addiction.
“I wrote an article,” he told Willie at the time. “My mom actually said, ‘You should send it to the New Yorker.’”
“The next day I got a call saying, ‘You know, we’ll give you 50 grand to write a book,’” he recalled. “I’m no dummy, I’m dunking french fries at age 44. I’ll write the d--- book.”
What Was Next for Bourdain After That?

The next stop was television. Following stints on the Travel Channel and Food Network, Bourdain turned his success into the long-running TV series “Parts Unknown,” in which he dove into the food of obscure places around the globe.

“Some delusional crackpots walked into the restaurant and offered me a TV show, and they showed up reeking of garlic, with a really bad attitude,” he recalled about how he wound up making shows about food and travel.

“I said, ‘I got a great idea. I travel around the world doing whatever I want in every cool place I ever dreamed of, and you pay. How’s that idea?’” he said. “And they were like, ‘Sounds like ... yeah. We’ll take 13 (episodes) of those.”
Bourdain Was Curious About Traveling Around the World
Bourdain was not afraid to get out of his comfort zone when it came to where he would visit.
“I’m not going full Geraldo (Rivera) out there in my flak jacket, poking my head up over a foxhole,” he said.
“But, you know, I’m curious about the world. And if there are manageable risks in return for satisfying my curiosity about a place, I’m willing,” he shared.
He Ate With Former President Barack Obama
Bourdain did sit down once with Barack Obama while he was president and remembered how he handled a potentially tricky question when he asked Obama how he felt about eating a hot dog with ketchup.

“Most people running for office would say, ‘Both ketchup and mustard, there are virtues, and I respect and admire people who...’ you know, get some wishy-washy answer to not piss off all the ketchup people. He said, ‘No, never!’” Bourdain recalled.
How Did Bourdain Choose Which Places to Spotlight?
For Bourdain, visiting an eatery, even if no one was familiar with it, came down to something very simple.

“The kind of questions we’re asking is, ‘Look, what does your soul crave at 2 o’clock in the morning when you got a little bit of a buzz?’ More often than not, that goes right to the heart of the culture,” he said.
Bourdain’s Daughter Was Not Afraid to Criticize His Cooking

Bourdain shared a daughter, Ariane, with ex-wife Ottavia Busia. She was 11 when he died, and Bourdain told Willie in their 2016 chat that she was tough as nails when it came to her reviews of his food.
“She’s brutal. I cannot get anything past her,” he said. “It’s like, ‘No, daddy, it’s too salty.’ ‘No, it’s not.’ Secretly, I know, yeah, she caught me. Every time.”
At the time, he also spoke about how his daughter inspired his new cookbook “Appetites: A Cookbook.”

title: ‘Wicker’ Movie Explained: Why Is the Internet Thirsting Over a Sentient Basket?
summary: What is the Wicker movie? Here’s the explanation of the Wicker movie, what it’s based on and the reaction to it.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the biggest headlines, leading with your questions. In this latest series, we’re breaking down why a movie about love and wicker sparked a big reaction.
The Scarecrow and the Tin Man better watch out, because there’s a new anthropomorphic leading man who has captured Hollywood’s attention … and he’s made of wicker.

Distributor Black Bear Pictures delighted and bewildered the internet on July 30 when it released the first trailer for an upcoming romantic fantasy comedy titled “Wicker,” out in theaters in the U.S. Oct. 23 and Oct. 30 in the UK. (The movie premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival in January.)

The film was first announced back in October 2023, when Variety reported that Oscar-winner Olivia Colman and Dev Patel were attached to a movie featuring an “unconventional romance.” But two years later, the publication announced Alexander Skarsgård would replace Patel, and that Peter Dinklage and Elizabeth Debicki were joining the cast, too.

A star-studded cast plus an intriguing plot seem like a recipe for a film worth checking out. But nothing could have prepared the internet for the first look, which showed Skarsgård’s full transformation into an unrecognizable man made of wicker.
Read on to find out why the internet is thirsting over Skarsgård’s twine-filled alter ego.
What Is ‘Wicker’ About?

As the film title implies, wicker is at the center of the story. The nearly two-and-a-half minute NSFW teaser that Black Bear Pictures debuted, which has already amassed over 1.5 million views, welcomes viewers to a seaside village where a fisherwoman, played by Colman, is ridiculed by members of the town.
Lonely and in need of a companion, the fisherwoman visits a local craftsman, portrayed by Dinklage, and requests that he make her a husband.
“Be at the chapel in a month,” he simply tells her.

After bending and molding endless sticks of twine, he creates her husband: Skarsgård’s wicker man. From head to toe, he is covered in wicker strands, which have been weaved and stitched together in various patterns across his body.
“I’m here to marry you,” Skarsgård’s character tells the fisherwoman upon seeing her. It’s safe to say she is pleased with the results.
The two begin their unusual love story, as some of the townspeople who previously mocked the fisherwoman now desire the same romance. Others are mortified and chaos ensues.
What Inspired ‘Wicker’?

“Wicker” was adapted from Ursula Wills-Jones’ short story “The Wicker Husband.” According to its Goodreads description, the 14-page story follows “an ugly girl who was short and dumpy, had one leg a bit shorter than the other, and her eyebrows met in the middle” — and she “wanted to marry.”
“Who will marry her while all the people made fun of her?” the premise asks. “Then, she married the wicker husband. what happened when she married him? What was the people’s reaction?”
In 2020, the story was turned into a folk musical that ran for a few weeks at the Watermill Theatre in Newbury, England.

A Facebook post from the theatre in March 2020 revealed that the production would use puppetry to bring the wicker man to life. “It is these puppets that steal the show,” recaps The Guardian’s three-star review of the show.
How Are Fans Reacting to the Trailer?
Fans’ reactions to the trailer have ranged from humorous posts about the plot to pure confusion to ... well, thirst with a side helping of surprise.
Beneath the YouTube trailer, fans left comments poking fun at the concept.
“Expected a horror film trailer, stayed for whatever this was,” one joked.
Another wrote, “Just when I think Alexander Skarsgard has finally achieved his weirdest role he comes at me with this.”
A third said, “I love that Peter Dinklage’s character is asked to make a Cottagecore Frankenstein and immediately says ‘say less.’”
Ikea joined in on the fun on Instagram by sharing a picture of a chair made of wicker with text that read “husband material.”
“We’ve got plenty of husband material,” the furniture company captioned the post before asking social media users to share how many times they watched the “Wicker” trailer.
A “Wicker” movie account responded, “No assembly required.”
To which Ikea cheekily replied, “Looking at our wicker furniture a little differently these days,” with a smirk emoji.
One Instagram user commented with an idea for the store. “And now all wicker items must be renamed to Skarsgård,” she wrote.
“Big Wick Energy,” another comment read.
Content creator JessAfterDark shared a hilarious Instagram video of her watching the trailer with her husband, who uttered, “Oh God!” when he saw Skarsgård’s character for the first time.
When the clip ended, he said he “couldn’t wait” to watch the movie.
Another Instagram user predicted that “baskets are about to make a huge comeback” on her page, adding “iykyk” (if you know you know).
In the caption she playfully wrote, “Alex Skarsgård… the basket that you are.”

title: A Hospital Patient Dreamed Of Attending A Metal Concert. So The Show Came To Him
summary: Tim Berry, a 27-year-old patient at Bruyère Health in Ottawa, Canada, recently wished to attend a metal concert but couldn’t leave the facility. So the show came to him.
story: Now *this* is metal.

Tim Berry, a 27-year-old patient at Bruyère Health in Ottawa, Canada, recently wished to attend a metal concert after receiving some difficult news about his health, clinical chaplain Roshene Lawson tells TODAY.com. While he was too medically fragile to leave the facility, Lawson pulled some strings to make magic happen.

With the help of staff and some kind folks at a local venue, Lawson threw a real metal show at the hospital in July, featuring band The Scepter, a whole lot of headbanging and, of course, that metalhead spirit.
Berry was able to rock out safely.

“Our clinical manager had told me he had some tears coming down during the concert,” Lawson says of Berry. “I went to ask him after. I said, ‘Were you crying because it was so loud?’ ... and he laughed and he said, ‘No, I’m really happy.’”

The Scepter played a 40-minute set for Berry, Lawson recounts. The band performed while fully decked out in their metal garb. They also set up their lights and blaring amps, along with some fans to blast their long locks, she says.
The Scepter’s Josh Collins explains that the band attempted to give Berry the most authentic experience they could.

“We wanted to give him a real show, not a watered down version because we were playing in a hospital,” he says. “It was emotional, for sure, but mostly we just felt privileged to be there and to play for him.”
Nurses painted Berry’s nails for the occasion and dressed him in a heavy metal shirt, Lawson adds. She even made tickets for the event, which patients used to attend the rock show.
“Everybody had to have their ticket to get in, and we tore the ticket, and they came in, and we had staff enjoying it with them,” Lawson says.

The chaplain explains that the idea for the concert came from a conversation she had with Berry after he was told about a change in his condition. She declined to disclose further medical details to protect Berry’s privacy.

“I went in and said to him, ‘Really, we can focus on this and how sad and frustrating it is, or we can focus on what you want to do with what’s left of life,’” Lawson recalls. “And he said, ‘I’d really, really like to go to a heavy metal concert.’”

Since Berry wasn’t cleared to leave the hospital, Lawson had to get creative. She called around and found Dominion Tavern, a spot that regularly hosts shows, and asked them for help. The business was more than happy to get on board, owner Scott McClinton says.
“I was in the unique position to be able to pull something like this off,” McClinton says. “I had most of the equipment, I know tons of bands and put on multiple shows weekly.”
It didn’t take long for McClinton to tap local band The Scepter for the performance, he says.

“They play straight-up epic, fun metal and always put on a great show,” McClinton says. “Plus I know a few of the members pretty well and they’re just really great, sweet dudes who I knew would say yes immediately – which was key as we didn’t have much time to organize all this.”
One of the trickiest aspects of the planning process, Lawson says, was finding the right spot to host such a raucous bash.

“It’s not quiet music, and we have other patients for whom that might not be their genre of music, so we had to find a place where we could put a proper concert on, where he could really live it as a concert,” Lawson says.
A conference room ended up being the perfect venue. And after moving around some furniture and setting up the band’s equipment, the scene was transformed, Lawson says.
“And honestly, the nurses, the recreation therapists, the physio, the OT, the clinical manager — everybody worked together to make this a fun thing for him,” Lawson adds.

While heavy metal isn’t always associated with comfort and peace, Lawson explains that it’s critical to meet patients’ unique needs. It’s especially important in a medical environment where there isn’t a lot of room to scream and shout and let it all out when you need to, she says.

“You and I could go home to our place, and if we’re having a bad day, just scream into a pillow or cry out loud or do whatever we need to do,” Lawson explains. “That’s harder to do when you’re in care.”

Lawson said that having a moment to rock out is “so cathartic, when you can really let that noise wash over you and it’s not the buzzing of the machines or the ringing of the call bells or the sound of the suction machine. It is bona fide living.”
The experience wasn’t just a memorable one for Berry. It’s also been impactful for McClinton, Lawson and all those involved.
“Getting to see Tim’s smile and the reaction from the staff is something that will stay with me for the rest of my life,” McClinton says.
He adds that “if you get a chance to help make someone’s day better, just do it.”
“It’ll be great for them and could be unbelievably rewarding for you,”  McClinton says.
The Scepter, whose members say they’ve felt moved by the concert as well, is also dedicating their next album to Berry.

“He brought us into something much bigger than we ever expected, and it feels right that he should be part of what comes next for us,” Collins says. “Dedicating the album to Tim is our way of recognizing him and what this experience has meant to the band.”
Rock on, Tim. Rock on.

title: Jason Sudeikis Shares How Ted Lasso Character Made Him A Better Dad
summary: In Apple TV’s “Ted Lasso,” the titular English football coach worships a hand-taped “Believe” sign like it’s scripture, simply cannot resist a folksy metaphor and thinks that a relentless stream of shortbread biscuits is the way to his boss’ heart.
story: In Apple TV’s “Ted Lasso,” the titular English football coach worships a hand-taped “Believe” sign like it’s scripture, simply cannot resist a folksy metaphor and thinks that a relentless stream of shortbread biscuits is the way to his boss’ heart.
For all of his quirks, Jason Sudeikis’ character Ted Lasso has taught the actor legitimate lessons about parenting, he told Willie Geist during the Aug. 9 episode of Sunday Sitdown.
“I think he’s a very sincere person, he accepts people where they are,” Sudeikis, 50, said.
“It’s made me a better parent,” he said. “I think there’s just a level of accountability that I think we love puttin’ on the show.”

After the Season 3 finale sent Ted back to Kansas City to coach his son’s team — a conclusion many viewers saw as the end of the show’s arc — Season 4 brought him right back across the pond. This time, he’s coaching a newly formed second-division women’s team.
In the new season, which premiered Aug. 5, Ted’s Lady Greyhounds encounter new challenges: sub-par facilities, less funding and skepticism toward women athletes.
Sudeikis acknowledged that “Ted Lasso” is, at its heart, a “silly fun show.” But still, its emotional resonance can carry real weight, he said.

“When a certain moment gets people and makes ‘em feel seen or it makes ‘em want to try or do something differently, it feels like a tremendous responsibility, ‘cause it’s bigger than me,” he explained.

Indeed, beneath the laughs of the first three seasons, Ted and the show’s other characters navigate mental health challenges, experience divorce and learn about what it means to actually lean on one another. The new season addresses other salient topics including the struggles that many women in sports continue to face.
Sudeikis opened up to the TODAY host about why the show pivoted to focus on a women’s team.

Production kicked around a few possibilities, he said, but nothing felt “as gooey” or “as juicy” as the storyline teased in the Season 3 finale, when a pitch for a Richmond women’s squad is first introduced.
The actor’s excitement for the show’s new twist was shaped in part by the women closest to him.
“I know how kick ass little girls are, having one of my own, but also, you know, growin’ up around a couple,” he told Willie.
He also added: “Being an older brother to two wise, funny, silly, authentic, heartfelt women, then-girls, now women — is baked into the enthusiasm for doing this new season.”

title: Chef Eric Ripert, One of Anthony Bourdain’s Closest Friends, Shares What It Was Like to Appear in ‘Tony’
summary: Eric Ripert tells TODAY.com how “Tony” portrays a different man than the public knew his late friend Anthony Bourdain to be. He also opens up about his cameo in the biopic.
story: If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988, or go to 988lifeline.org, to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. You can also call the network, previously known as the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, at 800-273-8255, or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

When chef Eric Ripert sat down to watch “Tony,” the biopic centered on the early life of his late close friend Anthony Bourdain, he didn’t recognize the man on the screen. He says that was a good thing.
